title: Rosh Hashanah: the world's birthday
hookLine: the new year marks the sixth day of creation, when people were made

cards: Most new year's celebrations are about a calendar turning over: a countdown, a ball dropping, a kiss at midnight. The Jewish new year sounds different in its prayers.
Right after the shofar is blown in the additional service, the congregation says a line in Hebrew: hayom harat olam. Today the world was conceived. Or born.
Not a calendar flipping. A birthday. And not the Jewish people's birthday.

teach.b: Rosh Hashanah means head of the year. Oddly, the Torah never uses that name. It calls the day the first of the seventh month, "a memorial proclaimed with the blast of horns, a holy convocation."
The rabbis gave it its well-known name. In the Talmud, two great sages argue about when the world was created.
Rabbi Eliezer says in the month of Tishrei, in the autumn. Rabbi Yehoshua says Nisan, in the spring. The prayer book follows Rabbi Eliezer for this day: the new year is the world's anniversary.
A midrash gets even more precise.

teach.h: THE SIXTH DAY: PEOPLE ARE MADE.
teach.b: If creation began on the twenty-fifth of Elul, then the first of Tishrei, Rosh Hashanah, is the sixth day, the day human beings were made.
It tells the first day of Adam's life hour by hour: created, given the breath of life, placed in the garden, given a command, broke it, judged, and pardoned, all before sunset.
And God says to him: this is a sign for your children. As you stood before Me in judgment today and went out pardoned, so will they, every year on this day.

So Rosh Hashanah holds two things at once: a day of judgment, solemn and serious, and a birthday party for the whole human race. Judgment, in this telling, happens to beloved creatures, on the day they were made.

how: Rosh Hashanah is observed on the first two days of Tishrei with long synagogue services, the shofar, festive meals with apples and honey and round challah, and the words 'today the world was born' after the shofar in Musaf.

practice: Picture the whole earth, not an idea of it but the actual oceans, a city at night, a crowded train, a baby being born somewhere right now, every one of them sharing this birthday.
If you pray, thank God for making the world and the people in it; if not, simply say it, quietly or out loud: happy birthday, world. Let it be as silly and as serious as it is.

wordCard.voice: Rosh Hashanah. Head of the year. The Jewish new year, remembered as the birthday of the world and the day people were made.

orig.note: Hebrew: today the world was conceived, said after the shofar on Rosh Hashanah.

carryVoice: Your line: happy birthday, world. A week of four thanks after eating, let us bless, every language, prayer shaping the day, the king in the field, thirty days to get ready. Day six hundred forty-four, done.
